title: Pushes, Pulls and Surfaces
seo_title: Year 3 Science: Pushes, Pulls and Surfaces Worksheets (Forces and Friction)
standard_text: Compare how things move on different surfaces. Notice that some forces need contact between two objects, but magnetic forces can act at a distance.
meta_desc: Free Year 3 science worksheets on forces: pushes and pulls, what forces do, contact and non-contact forces, and how things move on different surfaces. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A force is a push or a pull.
key_sub: Rough surfaces slow things more than smooth ones.
body_html:
How to think about it

A force is a push or a pull.

  • Forces can start or stop things, speed them up or slow them down, change their direction or shape.
  • Most forces need contact. Magnetism and gravity act at a distance.
  • Things move further on smooth surfaces, because rough surfaces cause more friction.
Example

Opening a drawer: push or pull?

It comes towards you

Answer: pull

Example

Ice or carpet: furthest?

Smoother, less friction

Answer: ice

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a moving thing has a force inside it.
  • Thinking smooth surfaces slow things more.
  • Thinking pulling a door is a push.

faq.a: A force is a push or a pull. Forces can make things start, stop, speed up, slow down, change direction or change shape.
A force where the two things touch, such as kicking a ball or friction. Magnetism and gravity are non-contact forces: they act at a distance.

faq.q: Why do things move further on smooth surfaces?
faq.a: Smooth surfaces have less friction, so less force slows the object down. Rough surfaces like carpet have more friction.
